doc.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Meeting Ruby Braff and Bobby Hackett while with McPartland
summary: At The Apartment he first met Ruby Braff, and he played on a Hackett tape of McPartland songs recorded at Fairchild House.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: There’s some nice quotes in a Jazz Times article that just came out, about her. Have you seen it yet?
I have it with me, we’ll take a look at it. It’s got you two or three times, talking about her.
Oh really? Oh good, I’d like to see that.
Yes, a marvelous lady. Was this at the Hickory House you played or was that after that?

No it was after that. The Hickory House had closed I think at that point. We worked at a place called The Apartment. The first time I met Ruby Braff was there. He came and sat in with us. And we had a great time traveling around together and playing. It gave me confidence in it. And Bobby Hackett — I actually met Bobby Hackett and played with him at that time. She was doing a Christmas present to a friend, somebody, I forget now, in Europe and she wanted to send a tape. So Hackett came in and read her songs and just, like an angel he played, just like an angel. “Yeah, Marian, nice tunes.” And Hank O’Neill
recorded it, it was at the Fairchild House. And for me it was like — I’d just come to New York and I’m playing with Marian and playing with Bobby Hackett, and it was real exciting.
Years later you played on a record of hers I have — “Ambiance?” There was some pretty adventurous playing on that.
